title: The LITTLE OWLS Study (in German: "Kleine Eulen OWL"): Exploring the Early-life Microbiome Development and Physical and Mental Health Outcomes During Childhood.
summary:
The LITTLE OWLS study is a prospective, longitudinal birth cohort study investigating early-life microbiome development and its association with physical and mental health outcomes during childhood. Recruitment began in 2024, enrolling families from late pregnancy through the child's first 6 years of life, with a target of at least 1000- 1200 children and their families.

The study characterizes longitudinal microbiome trajectories-including resilience and dysbiosis-and their relationship to common chronic diseases. Data are collected via online surveys, symptom and medication diaries, annual clinical exams, and repeated biological sampling of the child, mother, father/partner, siblings, and household environment. Findings are intended to support future diagnostics, prevention, and therapy for common chronic physical and mental diseases.
criteria:
Participation of both mother and child (newborn) is mandatory; participation of the father and siblings is optional.

Inclusion Criteria:

* mothers age ≥18 years at the time of enrollment
* newborn age: max. 14 days after birth at the time of enrollment
* sufficient proficiency in the study language (German)
* residence ≤ 40 km from Bielefeld city center, to ensure feasibility of long-term follow-up

Exclusion Criteria:

* no written study consent
* no ability to participate in the study (incl. self-sampling, online-questionnaires, study visits) according to the investigator´s instructions

sites.f: University Hospital OWL, Bielefeld University, Department for Pediatrics
